correctness.rationale: Independent rate-one mutant clocks reproduce the embedded colonization chain. Poisson edge thinning gives Exp(1/degree) passage times on the unique root paths. Conditioning on independent gamma far-time and common hub delay yields an exact finite binomial-gamma formula; a second Markov-chain recursion reproduces the exact fractions for k=1..17. An elementary k-th-moment inequality and Stirling yield an all-k exponential upper bound, so the infinite-family conclusion does not depend on finite tests. All assumptions, no-recovery limit, and degree normalization are stated.

The 2024 colonization paper examines expected times, not terminal-site probabilities. Background first-passage constructions are not claimed novel. value.rationale: The fixation-location distribution is a natural spatial extinction/colonization statistic not captured by mean colonization time. The originating article motivates the geographic-farthest heuristic and its failure in one cyclic example; the proposed exact example rules out the heuristic even for acyclic graphs with a unique farthest node and derives an exponentially strong, arbitrarily large family-level contrast. This is a meaningful structural boundary, not an arbitrary parameter perturbation or a numerical table re-computation.
